script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Workplace
Theme: second chances

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. MODERN ART GALLERY - DAY

A beautiful modern art gallery, filled with visitors, bustles with activity. A young ART DIRECTOR, JESSICA, in her late 20s, stands in the middle of it all, her eyes scanning the room. She's in her element, but a frown forms on her face as she notices a man, MIKE, standing near an exhibit. He's in his 40s, and though he seems out of place, there's an undeniable air of familiarity between them.

JESSICA
(to herself)
What is he doing here?

INT. MODERN ART GALLERY - OFFICE - DAY

Jessica sits in her small office, surrounded by artwork samples and posters. She's on the phone with an artist, negotiating a contract. She listens intently, nodding along.

ART DIRECTOR (JESSICA)
Yes, I understand your concerns. But I believe this exhibition will be a great opportunity for you. And I promise to do my best to make it work for both of us.

As she hangs up the phone, she lets out a sigh of relief. Her assistant, LUCAS, enters the room.

ASSISTANT (LUCAS)
Jessica, there's a man here who says he knows you. He insists on speaking with you.

Jessica's eyes widen, and she stands up, her mind racing.

JESSICA
Send him in.

INT. MODERN ART GALLERY - OFFICE - DAY

Mike enters the office, looking nervous. He hesitates before speaking.

MIKE
Jessica, it's been a long time. I didn't expect to see you here.

Jessica's expression is cold and unforgiving. She remembers all too well the mistakes he made in the past.

JESSICA
(skeptically)
What do you want, Mike?

MIKE
I want to make things right. I know I hurt you and the company in the past, and for that, I'm truly sorry. I've changed, I swear. I've been working on a new art project, and I believe it could be a great fit for your gallery.

Jessica crosses her arms, her skepticism clear.

JESSICA
And why should I believe you?

MIKE
Because I've proven myself. I've been working in the art world again, and I've earned the respect of my colleagues. I've even started my own art collective. I want a chance to show you my work and make amends.

INT. MODERN ART GALLERY - EXHIBITION ROOM - NIGHT

Weeks later, Jessica, Mike, and several other guests gather in the gallery for the opening of Mike's exhibition. The room is filled with beautiful, thought-provoking artwork. As Jessica walks through the crowd, she notices the way people are drawn to Mike's creations. She watches him engage with visitors, sharing stories and insights about his work.

Jessica approaches him, her expression softened.

JESSICA
(quietly)
Your work is incredible, Mike. I'm proud of you.

Mike turns to face her, surprised and touched.

MIKE
Thank you, Jessica. I couldn't have done it without your support, even if it was years ago.

Jessica smiles, and for the first time in a long while, she feels a sense of closure.

JESSICA
We all deserve second chances, don't we?

FADE OUT.

THE END
